samples.summary: `--panel-digest` short-circuits the new mixed-panel guard: a stated digest is never cross-checked against the digests the pooled envelopes actually record, so a pool spanning N panels can be filed under one panel identity without `--allow-mixed-panel`
samples.evidence: score-all.mjs:724 is `const panel = panelDigestArg ?? resolvePanelDigest({records: store.panelDigestRecords(ids), allowMixed})` — when `--panel-digest` is supplied the resolver (and therefore the whole refusal that this change exists to add) is never called. report.mjs:3369-3377 has the same shape: `resolvePanel` returns `{digest: args["panel-digest"], mixed: false, tally: []}` before `store.panelDigestRecords(runIds)` is ever read. Consequence: an operator (or any wrapper/workflow that passes the flag for the legitimate `not-recorded` case) files a cross-run score over runs whose envelopes record five different `panel_digest` values under a single `sha256:` segment, with `panel_digest_source: "reconstructed"` and — because `withPanelStamp` only adds `panel_digests` when `panel.mixed` is true (report.mjs:withPanelStamp) — no record of the mixture in the payload. `store.validateScorePanel` (store.mjs:474) cannot catch it either, since path and payload agree. The number then reads afterwards as one reviewer's, which the module header itself calls the defect. The asymmetry is visible one screen down in the same function: `--panel-sha` is unioned with the values read off the runs and a disagreement exits 1 (report.mjs:3477-3481); `--panel-digest` gets no such cross-check. Fix direction: resolve from the envelopes first, and treat a stated digest as an assertion to be reconciled (refuse when the runs state a different or multiple digests) rather than as a reason to skip reading them.

samples.summary: Operator CLI passes unvalidated `--at`/`--prefix` into `git show <at>:<prefix><rel>` with no `--`/`--end-of-options` separator and no ref grammar, so a value beginning with `-` is parsed by git as an option and a `../` prefix escapes the intended tree path
samples.evidence: panel-identity.mjs:518: `execFileSync("git", ["show", `${at}:${prefix}${rel}`], …)` where `at = flag("at")` and `prefix = flag("prefix")` come straight from argv (lines 514-515) with no shape check. Because the single argument is the whole `<rev>:<path>` string, an `at` beginning with `-` is consumed by git as an option rather than a revision — `git show` accepts diff options including `--output=<file>` (arbitrary file write of the diff output) and `--ext-diff` (runs external diff drivers configured in the repository being read). Separately, git treats `<rev>:./x` and `<rev>:../x` as CWD-relative rather than tree-root-relative, so `--prefix ../` reads a different tree location than the documented `scripts/agent/` while the printed `source` line still claims the prefix given. `execFileSync` with an argv array means there is no shell metacharacter vector, and today nothing but a human invokes this CLI (grepped: no workflow or script references panel-identity.mjs), so I could not complete an attacker-controlled chain — hence low-ish impact. Hardening: validate `at` against a ref grammar (and `prefix` against a path grammar), and pass `--end-of-options` / a leading `--` so a `-`-prefixed value can never be read as a git option.
searchedFor: grep for git show / execFileSync("git" call sites in scripts/

samples.summary: `tallyPanelDigests` accepts the reserved path-state strings `not-recorded`/`mixed` as values read off stored records, so an envelope on disk can assert a state instead of an identity and be pooled as one
samples.evidence: panel-identity.mjs:423 accepts a record whose `panelDigest` is any member of `PANEL_DIGEST_STATES`, not just a real digest: `if (!isPanelDigest(stated) && !PANEL_DIGEST_STATES.includes(stated))`. The states are outputs of the resolver and path-segment vocabulary, never legitimate envelope contents — `validateRunEnvelope` (store.mjs, `panel_digest must be sha256:<64 hex>`) refuses them on every store write, and store.test.mjs asserts that for `PANEL_DIGEST_ABSENT`. But `panelDigestRecords` reads whatever JSON is on disk (hand-edited files, externally ingested legacy items), so a record stating `panel_digest: "mixed"` yields `resolvePanelDigest` → `{digest: "mixed", mixed: false, tally: [one entry]}` with no opt-out required: report.mjs then stamps `panel_digest: "mixed"` without `panel_digests` and `validateScorePanel` refuses the write (store.mjs:495-501), stopping the lane; the render path instead names a `reports/…__mixed__….md` for a pool nothing detected as mixed. A record stating `not-recorded` likewise merges silently with genuinely-absent records, hiding one panel inside the absent bucket. Since the envelopes are the trust source for the pooling key, the read side should refuse these two strings from a record exactly as the write side does, and reserve them for resolver output only.

samples.summary: `panel_digests` is validated only when the path segment is `mixed`; a single-panel cross-run payload may carry an arbitrary `panel_digests` list that nothing checks or strips
samples.evidence: validateScorePanel returns at store.mjs:494 (`if (panelDigest !== PANEL_DIGEST_MIXED) return score;`) before looking at `score.panel_digests`, and report.mjs's `withPanelStamp` adds that key only for a mixed write and never removes an existing one — the payload arrives verbatim from `--from` (report.mjs:3404-3411, operator/scorer-supplied JSON). So a score filed under one real digest can ship a `panel_digests` list naming panels it never pooled, and a reader of the file on its own (the stated reason the panel travels in the payload at all) has no way to tell that list is bogus. Low impact — the producer is the lane's own scorers today — but the check is one line: refuse `panel_digests` on a non-mixed cross-run write, or require it to equal `[panelDigest]`.
searchedFor: read report.mjs withPanelStamp and the --persist path

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as quoted: score-all.mjs:724 short-circuits resolvePanelDigest via `??`, and report.mjs:3369-3377 returns a stated digest before store.panelDigestRecords is read, so the mixed-panel refusal is skipped and withPanelStamp (report.mjs:348-353) omits panel_digests because panel.mixed is false. However this is not a security defect under the Security rubric. (1) No trust boundary: the flag is only settable by whoever invokes the CLI, and .github/workflows/eval-score.yml:52-69 triggers only on workflow_dispatch (maintainer-only) and schedule and does not expose panel_digest as an input at all — the operator who could pass it already has direct write access to the eval store and could author any score file under any panel segment, so the override grants no privilege. (2) panel_digest is a content-identity/pooling key for benchmark score files (panel-identity.mjs:1-61, 480-488), not a signature, HMAC, or credential; nothing authenticates against it, and the override is logged on stderr (report.mjs:3375) and provenance-stamped `reconstructed`, enforced by store.mjs:487. (3) No injection/traversal: the value is regex-validated to `sha256:<64 hex>` before becoming a path segment (score-all.mjs:721-722, report.mjs:3371-3374, panel-identity.mjs:141). What is left is a data-integrity/consistency bug in an operator tool — one pooled number reading as a single reviewer's — which is the correctness lens's lane and explicitly deferred here. The reviewer's own evidence names the operator, not an attacker, as the actor, and I found no path by which an untrusted party influences the flag.
